property_summary: After giving an address its first bonus and calling withdrawReward, the recipient's external balance increases by exactly the reward amount and C holds no leftover payable balance for that recipient (i.e. contract balance decreases by that amount).
Calling withdrawReward on any recipient should never revert (i.e., always succeed).
Calling withdrawReward for any address that currently has a zero stored reward must not revert.

Calling withdrawReward(recipient) should not revert when the contract is not locked and the caller provides an address with a nonnegative stored reward (i.e., when rewardsForA[recipient] is read and setting it to a nonzero value is not required) — concretely: if the call is made while SmartFix._locked is false, withdrawReward must succeed (not revert).

Calling withdrawReward(recipient) must not revert when the contract is unlocked and the recipient address is able to receive the stored reward amount (i.e., the call succeeds), so reverted should be false whenever rewardsForA[recipient] equals the amount read and the recipient can accept Ether.

After calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient), the contract's rewardsForA[recipient] must be 0 (reference) but the mutant may leave it non-zero (set to 1) — so for all recipients rewardsForA becomes zero in the reference, and the mutant violates this for some recipient.

After any call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract, the stored rewardsForA[recipient] is zero (the reward is cleared); the mutant leaves a non-zero value (1) for some recipient, breaking this invariant.

For any recipient, after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) the correct contract always leaves the stored reward for that recipient equal to 0 (withdraw cleared); the mutant that sets the stored reward to 1 after reading breaks this invariant for some recipient.

For any recipient, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract always results in the contract's external balance decreasing by exactly the amount that was credited (i.e., the contract sends out the full reward and does not retain leftover wei), while the mutant that sets the stored reward to 1 after reading can cause the contract to retain 1 wei, breaking that invariant for some inputs.

For any recipient, after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) the contract's public getter for claimedBonus(recipient) becomes true (the bonus is marked claimed) — the mutant can revert the low-level payment causing claimedBonus to remain false for some recipient due to the altered stored-value during the external call.

For any recipient and any reward amount, after calling withdrawReward(recipient) the reference contract always clears rewardsForA[recipient] (leaving it zero), but the mutant that clears the balance only after the external call can leave rewardsForA[recipient] non-zero when the external call to recipient reverts or fails.

For any recipient and any reward amount, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the reference C always results in rewardsForA[recipient] being cleared (zero) after withdrawal even if the external call to recipient reverts; the mutant that clears rewardsForA only after the external call can leave rewardsForA[recipient] non-zero when the recipient's fallback reverts, so the property is violated for some recipient that reverts on receive.

For any recipient and any reward amount, if withdrawReward is invoked and the external call to the recipient REVERTS, the reference contract still clears rewardsForA[recipient] (leaving it zero) while the mutant that clears only after the external call will leave rewardsForA[recipient] non-zero (the test detects this by observing that after a failing external transfer, calling withdrawReward again will revert on the reference due to zero payout but will behave differently on the mutant because rewardsForA remains non-zero).

For any recipient contract that re-enters during the external call, the reference C's withdrawReward always resets rewardsForA[recipient] to 0 before allowing reentrancy protection to end, so a reentrant attacker cannot extract more than the recorded reward; the mutant that clears rewardsForA only after the external call allows a reentrant attacker to observe a nonzero reward and withdraw it again, violating this invariant.

For any recipient contract that reverts when sent ETH, the reference C always leaves rewardsForA[recipient] cleared (0) after withdrawReward even if the external call fails, whereas the mutant that zeroes the balance only after the external call can leave rewardsForA[recipient] non-zero when the external transfer to the recipient reverts.

After withdrawReward(recipient) returns successfully, the stored rewardsForA[recipient] is zero in the correct contract for all inputs; the mutant that omits resetting rewardsForA[recipient] can leave a nonzero stored reward for some inputs (e.g., when amount>0).

For any caller/recipient, after withdrawReward returns the contract remains unlocked so a subsequent withdrawReward call can be made (i.e. the second call does not revert); the mutant that never clears _locked will make a second call revert for some inputs (when the first call succeeds).

For any recipient address and amount fuzzed as the initial reward, calling getFirstWithdrawal(recipient) on the correct contract will always leave the contract _nonReentrant lock cleared (so a subsequent withdrawReward(recipient) call will NOT revert), while the mutant that never clears the lock will make that subsequent withdraw attempt revert for some inputs (specifically when the first sequence succeeds).

For any recipient and initial reward value, calling withdrawReward on the reference C never permanently blocks future calls (i.e. a subsequent withdrawReward to the same recipient succeeds), whereas the mutant that omits clearing the reentrancy lock can leave the contract permanently locked so a later withdrawReward call will revert for some inputs (when the first call succeeds).

For any recipient address and any initial reward amount, calling getFirstWithdrawal(recipient) on the correct contract always results in the contract remaining unlocked so that a subsequent external call from an attacker contract (which re-enters via receive) can successfully call withdrawReward(recipient) again; the mutant that never clears the reentrancy lock leaves the contract locked and thus causes the re-entrant withdraw to revert for some inputs.

For every recipient and attacker payoff, calling getFirstWithdrawal(recipient) on the correct contract always results in the external low-level call returning false (i.e., the low-level call to recipient fails) being observed as a failed withdraw (catchable), while the mutant that leaves the reentrancy lock set will change whether that external call can be observed as failing for some fuzzed recipient/attacker combinations (the observable revert/ok of withdrawReward differs).

Reference C ensures that during withdrawReward the reentrancy lock remains set until after the external call returns (preventing reentrant calls from observing/consuming the reward), whereas the mutant releases the lock early allowing a reentrant caller to re-enter withdrawReward and drain the reward resulting in a different post-call balance/state.

For any recipient contract, after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) the reference C always results in rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 (the bonus is immediately withdrawn and cannot be drained by reentrancy), whereas the mutant that releases the lock early allows a reentrant recipient to re-enter withdrawReward and observe/drain a nonzero reward leaving rewardsForA[recipient] != 0 for some inputs.

For any recipient contract, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract always results in withdrawReward having completed with no remaining rewards (address(c).balance decreased by 100 and withdraw returned success), while the mutant that releases the lock early can be re-entered by a malicious recipient causing the final withdraw to fail or leave rewards nonzero for some recipient addresses.

For any recipient contract, invoking getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract always results in rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 after the call (the bonus is withdrawn exactly once and cannot be drained by reentrancy); the mutant that releases the lock early allows a reentrant recipient to re-enter withdrawReward and leave rewardsForA[recipient] != 0 for some recipient contracts/inputs.

For any recipient contract that performs a reentrant call during receive(), the reference C guarantees that after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) the contract's balance decreased by exactly 100 and rewardsForA[recipient] is 0 (the bonus is fully withdrawn and cannot be double-withdrawn by reentrancy), whereas the mutant that releases the lock early can be reentered and cause the final contract balance to be greater than expected (i.e. not decreased by 100) for some recipient attacker contracts.

Calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) always leaves rewardsForA[recipient] == 0 after it returns and either sends funds or reverts (i.e., no leftover reward balance visible via withdraw attempts).
Calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus on any recipient never reverts (i.e., it always completes) on the original contract.
For any recipient who has not yet claimed the bonus, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus never reverts (reverted == false).
Calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus on a not-yet-claimed recipient should not revert (reverted == false).
For a recipient address that satisfies the test preconditions, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) should not revert (reverted == false).

For any recipient, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract either fully succeeds and leaves claimedBonus[recipient]==true only if the external withdrawReward call succeeded, or reverts and leaves claimedBonus[recipient]==false; the mutant that sets claimedBonus before the external call can leave claimedBonus==true even when the external withdraw fails (observable via a failing external callee), so the invariant is violated for some inputs.

For any recipient and any external callee behavior, a successful call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus only marks claimedBonus[recipient] true if withdrawReward completed successfully; the mutant sets claimedBonus before the external call and thus can mark it true even when the external call reverts (e.g., a reverting recipient), violating this invariant.

For any recipient, a successful call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus(address) on the correct contract results in claimedBonus[recipient] == true only when the external withdrawReward completed successfully; the mutant that sets claimedBonus before the external call can leave claimedBonus[recipient] == true even if the external withdraw fails (e.g., when the recipient contract reverts).

For any recipient, after calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract, either the call reverts and claimedBonus[recipient] remains false, or the call succeeds and claimedBonus[recipient] is true; the mutant can set claimedBonus to true even when the external withdrawReward call fails (reverting callee), breaking this rule.

After any call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient), the correct contract either reverts leaving claimedBonus[recipient]==false, or (on success) leaves claimedBonus[recipient]==true; the mutant that sets claimedBonus before the external withdraw can make claimedBonus true even when the external withdraw reverts (via a reverting recipient), violating this rule.
After calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) the recipient's address balance increases by exactly 100 wei (withdrawn bonus).

property_summary: Calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus for any address that has not yet claimed must always revert (original requires the bonus to be available and withdraw fails otherwise), so reverted must be true for all such recipients.
The original contract always reverts (the call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus should fail) for any recipient on the first call.
The original contract always reverts on the first call to getFirstWithdrawalBonus for any recipient (i.e., the call must fail and reverted == true).
The original contract's getFirstWithdrawalBonus call should always revert (so reverted == true) when invoked from this test under the precondition.

For any recipient address, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract always increases address(c).balance decreased by 100 transferred out to recipient (i.e., the contract's balance decreases by 100 when recipient can receive), whereas the mutant that adds 0 will not decrease the contract balance by 100 for some recipient — the test detects that difference by funding the contract and invoking getFirstWithdrawalBonus for a recipient that can accept Ether.

For any recipient that can receive ETH, calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus(recipient) on the correct contract always decreases address(c).balance by 100 (the contract pays the bonus and withdraws it), whereas the mutant that increments rewards by 0 will not decrease address(c).balance by 100 for some recipient — the test fuzzes the recipient and initial contract funding to find such a case.

If a caller has not yet claimed the bonus, then calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus causes the recipient's external balance to increase by exactly 100 (the bonus) when starting from zero contract payout for that recipient.
